clue.text: Bum runs into tree

indicators.note: the runs abbreviation is placed into the tree, so the tree's letters close round it

parts.note: a beech is a common broadleaf tree
R is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Someone's backside collides with a tree trunk.
explanation.definitionFit: A breech is an old word for the buttocks, as in a breech birth, bottom first.

clue.text: PM's 17 book 5 20 3 16 across

definitions.meaning: the 's stands for 'is': a former British Prime Minister, Arthur, is the first sense
with the cross-references filled in this reads 'behind the book Pretty Girl in Crimson Rose', naming the crossword memoir's author, Sandy

explanation.walkthrough: Fill in the numbers: 17 gives 'behind the', 5 PRETTY, 20 GIRL IN, 3 CRIMSON, 16 across ROSE. Sandy Balfour wrote the memoir 'Pretty Girl in Crimson Rose (8)', and Arthur Balfour was Prime Minister 1902-05.
explanation.definitionFit: Shared surname: Arthur Balfour led the Conservative government, while Sandy Balfour wrote the crossword memoir named in the cross-references.

clue.text: See 17
Remake of modernistic film

indicators.note: a remake reworks earlier material, so the letters of the next word are made again in a new order

explanation.surface: A new version of a modern-style movie is being shot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Remake' looks like film jargon to go with 'film', but it signals rearranging MODERNISTIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Crimson Tide is a 1995 submarine thriller starring Denzel Washington and Gene Hackman.

clue.text: Optimistic conductor raises his baton for this

definitions.meaning: cheerful and hopeful about the future

definitions.text: conductor raises his baton for this
definitions.meaning: the unaccented beat before the bar line is shown by the conductor's upward stroke

explanation.definitionFit: Upbeat means cheerful, and in music it is the beat marked by the conductor's raised hand.

clue.text: See 22
Up before most others, he barely troubled the writer on the way

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sitting on another is placed above it
troubled means disturbed or stirred up, so the letters of barely are thrown into a new order

parts.note: the writer is the setter, who refers to himself as I
RD is the abbreviation for road, a way

explanation.surface: A man who rises early is hardly bothered by the author on his route.
explanation.walkthrough: 'he' belongs to the definition: the early riser is a person. 'on' works because this is a down clue, so the setter sits above the road.
explanation.definitionFit: An early bird is a person who gets up or arrives sooner than other people.

clue.text: Touching behaviour concealed by hat

indicators.note: something concealed by a covering sits inside it, so the hat holds the behaviour word

parts.note: tile is old slang for a hat, especially a top hat
tact is considerate, diplomatic behaviour

explanation.surface: Affectionate gestures are hidden beneath someone's headgear.
explanation.walkthrough: TILE as a hat is dated British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Tactile describes something perceived through touch or a person given to physical contact.

clue.text: Innuendo from Belgium and one other

definitions.text: Innuendo from Belgium and one other

parts.words: Innuendo from Belgium and one other
parts.note: a suggestive remark has a second, rude sense; here a word meant as Belgium and as one other thing at once is pictured

explanation.definitionFit: Innuendo works by giving words a second, usually smutty, sense alongside the innocent one.

clue.text: So-called good walk spoiled over strike

indicators.note: over is used for something turned back, so the game is read from its end

parts.note: a quip attributed to Mark Twain calls golf a good walk spoiled

explanation.surface: A ruined stroll is blamed on a strike.
explanation.definitionFit: To flog is to beat or whip, which is to strike repeatedly.

clue.text: Is harbouring a little brief deception in strengthening system

indicators.note: a harbour shelters ships within it, so the two letters of Is enclose the rest

parts.note: some means a small amount

indicators.note: brief means cut short, so the last letter of the deception word is dropped

parts.note: a trick is a deception

explanation.surface: A small brief lie lurks in a fitness regime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a little' looks like it should shorten something, but it is a synonym; 'brief' does the trimming, and 'harbouring' wraps Is around the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Isometrics is a method of exercise building muscle by pushing against a fixed resistance.

clue.text: Stars show contempt for educational paper

parts.note: to boo is to jeer in contempt
TES is the Times Educational Supplement, a British weekly for teachers

explanation.surface: Celebrities sneer at a teachers' newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: The TES is a British weekly newspaper for teachers.
explanation.definitionFit: Bootes, the Herdsman, is a northern constellation, a group of stars containing Arcturus.

clue.text: 0 or 1 squared in small steps

parts.note: a binary digit, a bit, is either 0 or 1
squared means multiplied by itself, so the word is followed by 'by' and itself again

explanation.surface: A binary digit is raised to the second power, gradually.
explanation.walkthrough: As 'three squared' is three by three, a bit squared is the same word, 'by', and the word again.
explanation.definitionFit: Bit by bit is an idiom meaning gradually, a little at a time.

clue.text: Front man now here, he's gone

parts.note: the present is now, the current time

indicators.note: the 's stands for 'is', and he is gone means those two letters are removed

parts.note: taken as written before the two letters are removed
taken as written as the letters to remove

explanation.surface: The leading man is present one moment and gone the next.
explanation.walkthrough: 'he's gone' removes H and E from HERE, leaving ER.
explanation.definitionFit: A presenter fronts a television or radio programme, hence front man.

clue.text: Rope-maker's little sibling on top of mountain, negotiating border

indicators.note: in a down clue the sibling is placed on top of what follows

parts.note: sis is a short informal word for sister

indicators.note: negotiating means making a way through, so the border runs through the mountain

parts.note: an alp is a high mountain
a hem is a border of cloth

explanation.surface: A small sister on a peak crosses the frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: HEM goes through ALP to make ALHEMP, under SIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Sisal hemp is a strong plant fibre traditionally twisted into rope and twine.

clue.text: See 3
See 26
Oscar — person found in drowned valley here

indicators.note: found in means placed inside, so Oscar and the person sit within the valley word

parts.note: a ria is a long inlet formed when a river valley is flooded by the sea
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a man is a person

explanation.surface: An Oscar-winner is discovered in a flooded valley in this place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'here' points to the country itself as the place where all this happens.
explanation.definitionFit: The definition 'here' stands for a place, and Romania is the country where the wordplay is set.

clue.text: Being in uncomfortable position in pool woefully heightened bath bill

definitions.text: Being in uncomfortable position in pool

indicators.note: woefully means badly or wretchedly, so the letters that follow are put into a poor new order

explanation.surface: An enormous bill for a bath has been sadly inflated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'woefully' rearranges HEIGHTENED BATH BILL. The phrase comes from pool, where a ball stuck behind the black eight ball is hard to play.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for being in a difficult spot comes from pool, where the black ball blocks a shot.

clue.text: One is engaged in continuous action, making air cleaner

parts.note: one is I as a Roman numeral

indicators.note: engaged in means held within, so the small word sits inside the action

parts.note: a oner is film jargon for a scene shot in one continuous take
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is busy with ongoing work that purifies the atmosphere.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'oner' is a single uncut shot in film-making.
explanation.definitionFit: An ioniser is a device that charges air particles to clean the air.

clue.text: One who perpetrates swindle right after sleuth's elucidation

indicators.note: after means the right abbreviation follows the rearranged letters
an elucidation works something out, so the detective's letters are sorted into a new order

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A detective's explanation exposes a conman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elucidation' signals rearrangement because a sleuth's explanation sorts out the jumbled facts; 'after' puts the right abbreviation last.
explanation.definitionFit: A hustler is a con artist who cheats people out of money.

clue.text: A diamond grinding factory, in original — unusual — setting

indicators.note: a setting holds a gem, so the rearranged letters hold the factory word
unusual means out of the ordinary, so the letters are put into an unexpected order

parts.note: a mill grinds grain

explanation.surface: A gem is cut at a factory and placed in a novel mount.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges the ten letters of in and original, and that 'setting', like a ring's mount for a gem, holds the factory word.
explanation.definitionFit: A diamond, said of a person, is a rare gem, and a girl in a million is a rare and excellent woman.

clue.text: See 20
Like Helen of Troy, or the pride of London?

definitions.meaning: of unmatched beauty, as the legendary Helen was
London pride is a saxifrage, a garden plant also known by this phrase

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means more beautiful than any other, and it is also a folk name for the London pride plant.

clue.text: Smart old boy born in the Big Apple

indicators.note: in places the old boy and born inside the city abbreviation

parts.note: the Big Apple is New York, abbreviated NY
OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil

explanation.surface: A stylish former pupil was born in New York.
explanation.walkthrough: An old boy is a former pupil of a British school.
explanation.definitionFit: Nobby is dated British slang for smart or elegant.

clue.text: Stresses, eg swapping for these subordinates

indicators.note: swapping means exchanging, so the e of the first word is traded for the g

parts.note: to stress a point is to underline it, so stresses means underlines

explanation.surface: Emphasis is placed on, for example, exchanging these junior staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eg' is not 'for example' here but the two letters: E is swapped for G.
explanation.definitionFit: Underlings are people of lower rank who serve under others.

clue.text: See 17
Playwright's fallen into beer plant down the slope

indicators.note: something fallen into a drink sits inside it, so the playwright goes into the beer

parts.note: ale is a kind of beer
Arthur Wing Pinero was an English playwright; with the 's he gives his name plus S

explanation.surface: A dramatist has tumbled drunkenly into his beer.
explanation.walkthrough: Pinero wrote 'The Second Mrs Tanqueray'. 'down the slope' is a jokey hint at a mountainside flower.
explanation.definitionFit: The alpine rose is a shrub of mountain slopes, such as the Alps' rhododendron.

clue.text: Worship by consuming fish

indicators.note: consuming means eating, so the by word swallows the fish

parts.note: per means by, as in per hour
a ray is a flat fish

explanation.definitionFit: A prayer is an act of worship addressed to a god.
